name: Camera-based deck activity monitor

source.document: Team-defined Logitech BRIO 101 USB camera prototype running CPU OpenCV on Dell Snapdragon X Elite; not an official Annex B guest.
assumptions_added: All onboard power, mass, placement, bandwidth, compute and installation figures are demonstration assumptions, not verified ship or camera measurements.
0.5 kg represents a hypothetical ship-mounted camera and bracket, not the laptop.
0.1 kW is a synthetic reservation for the entire camera/processing system, not the BRIO 101's measured USB power.
Mast-slot placement is simulated; live webcam is connected to a separate Dell prototype.
0.01 Mbit/s models status metadata only. Raw video is not sent over the simulated ship network.
One crew member and 30 minutes for port installation are hypothetical demonstration values, not an installation authorization.

capability.description: Observes movement within a marked simulated deck area and provides non-safety-certified crew advisory events.

configurations.notes: Hypothetical use of the one free mast slot; may compete with G1/G5. Physical mounting is not verified.

power_modes.notes: Synthetic sustained 0.1 kW reservation, not measured camera draw.

cooling.notes: Hypothetical mast air cooling; 1:1 electrical-to-heat convention.

data_links.notes: Local activity-event metadata only, not camera frames.

operational_modes.notes: OpenCV motion detector reports moving pixels in a marked region; absence of motion never certifies deck clearance.

installation.notes: Hypothetical one-person 30-minute port-only install for solver demonstration; not a real installation certificate.

policy_hints: G7 alerts are advisory only; never infer safe deck clearance from NO_MOVEMENT_DETECTED.
Camera failure or stale data is UNKNOWN, not safe.
Do not trigger G6 fire suppression or G4 flight authorization from G7.
documented_unknowns: Real onboard camera placement, power including host computer, weather tolerance and installation details unknown.
OpenCV motion detection can miss stationary objects, fail under glare or in darkness, and cannot identify persons reliably.
Actual deck-safety logic and Scenario D trigger conditions are not yet defined.
Real per-guest hardware requirements and processing-latency limits remain unverified.
notes: User-defined G7; physical values model hypothetical shipboard adoption, live camera runs on a Dell development laptop.
The live JSON event stream does not automatically affect D1–D4 or safety interlocks.
